key_insight: TryOnCrafter turns video virtual try-on from a camera-passive task into a camera-controllable one, enabling realistic garment rendering from new viewpoints. It does this by introducing a renderable 4D try-on proxy that supports interactive omnidirectional view exploration.
problem_solved: Existing video virtual try-on methods are tied to the source video's camera trajectory, so users cannot freely change viewpoint or explore the subject from different angles. This paper addresses the lack of camera control in video-based clothing synthesis.
method: Defines a new task setting called Camera-controllable Video Virtual Try-on (CaM-VVT).
Builds a renderable 4D try-on proxy to represent the dressed person across space and time.
Uses the proxy to synthesize realistic try-on results under arbitrary camera trajectories for interactive viewpoint control.
impact: This matters because it moves virtual try-on closer to practical, interactive applications such as fashion browsing, immersive e-commerce, and AR/VR fitting experiences. For AI/ML practitioners, it highlights a new direction for controllable video generation beyond fixed-view synthesis.

paper_title: TryOnCrafter: Unleashing Camera Trajectories for Realistic Video Virtual Try-on via a Renderable 4D Try-on Proxy
paper_authors: Hao Sun, Hao Yan, Mengting Chen, Quanjian Song, Yu Li
